newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips PCC chief sees fast revenue growth.
newsitem.headline: Philips PCC chief sees fast revenue growth.

text.p: PCC, Philips Electronics NV's consumer telephone-making venture with Lucent Technologies, can grow its revenues by much more than market growth rates, its chief said Monday.

"I would expect the future revenues of the business to grow much faster than the market growth. We're going to be in the top three (in the world market) by the year 2000," PCC Chief Executive Mike McTighe told reporters at a briefing.
Philips and Lucent said last week they were merging their consumer communications products businesses into the 60/40 PCC venture, which would have annual sales of $2.5 billion.
"Last year the market we're talking about was in excess of $20 billion and it's growing at around 15 percent per annum in revenue terms," McTighe said.
The market was set to boom as sales of personal communications equipment rocketed, driven by the demand for mobile communications, particularly cellular phones, he said.
Mobile phone ownership at the end of last year was around 1.6 percent of the world's population, McTighe said.
"We haven't seen the market yet. That's not the penetration you would expect of a normal consumer device," he said, noting the figure was 28 percent in Scandinavia.
He said Philips chairman Cor Boonstra had been closely involved in the Lucent talks which had kicked off "literally a few weeks ago."

"It's all part of the (Boonstra) strategy. He's always believed we needed a growth strategy -- restructuring is absolutely necessary and will continue to be necessary -- but you can't run a business just on restructuring, you have to grow," McTighe said.
